sections.name: mission
sections.value:
You build ALL THREE units of plan 093 in one wave: u1 rs-client, u2 rs-records, u3 rs-events. There is NO PM on this plan — you report to the PRIME (chainglass o-prime). Settle u1's interface FIRST and do not start u2 or u3 until it is settled, because both sit on it.

What you are replacing and why it matters: chainglass currently reads the pij fleet by SPAWNING A PROCESS per tick. That call now takes 7.744s against a 5s timeout, so every call is killed before it returns — the loop paid ~95% of a core continuously and received NOTHING. It is switched off. You are building the reader that replaces it. pij-rs answers the same question in 113ms over HTTP.

value.text: Orient: read impl-guide.dd.json (your three unit rows, the HARD CONSTRAINTS, the composition steps), plan.dd.md, and assets/backpressure.dd.json — the backpressure rows ARE your done bar. Then `harness boot --json` in your worktree before changing anything.

ACK BEFORE CODE, and the ack is a REVIEW OF MY DOCUMENT, not a receipt. Reply with a numbered plan, and correct anything in the impl-guide you find wrong with evidence — a wrong file pointer, an interface that cannot be implemented as written, a false premise about the daemon. I would rather be corrected now than have you build around my mistake.

DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE3: for every meaning-shaped question ('where is X handled', 'what owns Y') run `flowspace3 search` or `ask` BEFORE grep. USE `--source code` — this repo carries a very large docs/plans/** corpus and the default blend buries code under prose ABOUT the code; I asked 'where does chainglass implement the pij records interface' and the correct file did not appear at all unscoped, then scored 1.0 with --source code. Report misses and confusing envelopes to me; they are worth more than hits. NOTE 2026-09-02: flowspace3 is DEGRADED (host disk filled, postgres down) — every query may return FS3-E-STORE-QUERY-FAILED. That is a known outage, NOT a product finding: do not report it, and do not conclude a file is unindexed from it. Use grep while it is down and re-try fs3 later.

The daemon is LIVE at 127.0.0.1:7461 and you should use it while building: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.pij-rs/daemon.key)" http://127.0.0.1:7461/v1/seats`. Do not guess the wire shape from the packet — the packet was already wrong once (it documented /v1/state as GET; it is POST {"id":...}, verified 405 on GET).

PROVE, DO NOT ASSERT. Each backpressure row's proof is a COMMAND with an exit status. Run them and paste real output in your done report. bp-0006 (401 -> exactly one re-read) must be exercised against the REAL daemon using a scratch PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR and a rotated key file — a mocked 401 proves the branch exists, not that the daemon accepts what you re-read. bp-0004 (a closed seat DISAPPEARS within 2s) is the row most likely to be skipped and the one that matters most: a reader that only ever sees appearances has not been proven to track truth.

STOP AND ASK me rather than guessing on: any change to IPijRecords (if a consumer must change, the seam was wrong and that is my problem, not yours to patch); any new dependency; anything that would require a write to pij-rs; and any temptation to flip the default to rs.
I am the prime and your only interface — there is no PM on this plan. Message me for acks, questions and the done report.
DEFER to me: interface changes, dependency additions, anything touching the flip. I defer product questions to Jordan.
Ask early and in one message rather than late in three. A blocked seat that waits silently costs more than a question.

value.fence: apps/web/src/features/089-first-class-pij/server/rs/** and test/unit/web/pij/rs-*.test.ts. Plus ONE line at the construction site in start-pij-poller.ts for the PIJ_SOURCE selection, and only that.
value.forbidden_note: NEVER work in /Users/jordanknight/substrate/chainglass — that is the main checkout and the prime is live in it. Never touch .harness/government/**. Never merge; I merge. Do not create worktrees; yours is scaffolded. Do not import from the pij repo (~/pi-hacking/pij) — chainglass must build with it absent; the reference file is vendored at assets/inputs/ for SHAPE only.

value.text: All three unit interfaces implemented as written in the impl-guide, or amended by me on your ack.

Unit tests pass standalone and pin every mapped field AND every explicit gap (watchdog/bindHealth/degraded/role). A test that only checks the happy fields passes on a mapping that quietly defaults watchdog to a plausible value — that is the defect this row exists to catch.
`just fft` green in your worktree with PIJ_SOURCE unset (bp-0008). There is no 'unrelated failure' exception in this repo — a red check is red; stop and ask me.

Every backpressure row run against the LIVE daemon with real output pasted in the done report. Rows you could not run: say so explicitly and why. An unrun row reported as green is the only unrecoverable failure here.
Default unchanged: PIJ_SOURCE unset or =legacy behaves exactly as before.
